department: Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (School of Engineering)

deadline.value: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, with an approximate fall deadline of June 15.

gre_general.value: The GRE is not required, but a score is welcome.
gre_general.quote: Results from the GRE are not required. However, candidates are welcome to submit a score in support of their application.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: The page asks for a statement of research and a resume but does not say a faculty agreement is needed first.

funding.value: International applicants face a limited, selective and competitive assistantship process, and Dayton offers no international doctoral aid or merit scholarships.
funding.quote: Please note the assistantship process is limited, selective and competitive.

entry_route.value: Applicants need an undergraduate degree in engineering, physics, chemistry, applied mathematics or a related field.
entry_route.quote: Applicants must have an undergraduate degree from an accredited program in engineering, physics, chemistry, applied mathematics or other appropriate program of study.

notes: Covers Mechanical Engineering D.E. and Ph.D. The Aerospace Engineering D.E. and Ph.D. (udayton.edu/academics/programs/aerospace-engineering-de-phd/index.php) has the same June 15 fall deadline and optional GRE. The international page lists the Mechanical and Aerospace Ph.D.s among programs that may require the GRE or GMAT; the department pages say the GRE is not required, so the department rule is used. The Mechanical page sets a 3.5 GPA and the Aerospace page 3.0.
name: Mechanical Engineering D.E., Ph.D.
